entries.name: Adobe pueblo (Taos style)
layout: steps like bleachers toward the plaza
no windows on the ground floor
ladders from terrace to terrace
kiva dug into the plaza side
entries.found: still inhabited pueblos of the Rio Grande valley, New Mexico
entries.notes: Read as one mass with a pixelated stepped silhouette; the viga ends are the tell. Cool inside, party house on every roof.

entries.name: Bedouin black tent (beit al-sha'ar)
parts: front men's side and back women's side
wind wall on the lee side
layout: a long rectangle, ridge pole high in the middle
the back wall faces the wind
camel pens and cook fire outside
blueprint: layer 0: b b b b b b b b b|b . . . . . . . b|b . . . . . . . b|b . . . . . . . b|b b b d d d b b b
legend: b black goat-hair wall, d open entrance, . air
entries.found: desert camps near wells and pasture, seasonally mobile
entries.notes: Woven from black goat hair, it tightens and sheds rain when wet. A camp can be packed and gone inside the hour.

entries.name: Moroccan riad
layout: life turns inward around the courtyard
guest rooms downstairs, family upstairs
no ground-floor windows to the street
entries.found: the medina quarters of Marrakech, Fez and Rabat
entries.notes: Invisible from the street: all the wealth is in the courtyard. Fountain sound masks voices, which is the point.

entries.name: Andalusian cortijo
layout: long main block facing a yard
agricultural wings attached
white walls throw off the Andalusian sun
entries.found: olive groves and dehesas of Andalusia, southern Spain
entries.notes: The white-on-ochre look is survival, not decoration. Usually lone house plus outbuildings; nearest neighbour far off.

entries.name: Mexican hacienda
layout: life organized around a succession of patios
chapel attached or inside the complex
walls high, openings small
entries.found: the dry altiplano and Bajio of central Mexico
entries.notes: Half palace, half factory; many are now hotels but the plan is unchanged: chapel, great house, work yard.

entries.name: Cycladic cube house
layout: stacked against neighbours into terraced villages
narrow shaded lanes
roof collects every drop of rain
entries.found: Mykonos, Santorini, Naxos and the other Cyclades, Greece
entries.notes: White reflects the sun, blue trim is naval. Cubic form reads beautifully in voxels; roofs double as streets in dense villages.

entries.name: Apulian trullo
layout: single conical room, sometimes two joined
cone channels rainwater off the base
tiny low door, cool dark interior
blueprint: layer 0: . s s s s s .|. s . . . s .|. s . . . s .|. s . . . s .|. s . . . s .|. s . . . s .|. s s d s s .
layer 1: . . c c c . .|. c c c c c .|. c c c c c .|. c c c c c .|. c c c c c .|. c c c c c .|. . c c c . .
legend: s limestone wall (whitewashed), c corbelled cone stone, p finial pinnacle, d door (south), . air
entries.found: Itria valley around Alberobello, Puglia, Italy
entries.notes: Dry-stacked so it could be knocked down when tax inspectors came. The cone-on-cube silhouette is unforgettable.

entries.name: Nubian tukul
layout: domed main room, cooler than any flat roof
flat-roofed rooms joined for stores
painted stripes and colour patches outside
entries.found: Nubian villages along the Nile in Aswan governorate, Egypt, and northern Sudan
entries.notes: The Nubian vault (mudbrick catenary without formwork) was revived by Hassan Fathy; domes survive heat better than flat roofs.

entries.name: Sana'a tower house
parts: 5 to 8 storeys, tan brick with white friezes
storage and animals on the ground floor
layout: ground floor for goods and animals
family floors above, best rooms top
roof terrace behind a parapet
entries.found: the old city of Sana'a, Yemen (UNESCO)
entries.notes: The stone-to-brick gradation (heavy below, light above) is structural engineering you can see. White friezes are lime, not paint.

entries.name: Persian badgir (windcatcher) house
parts: basement sardab cooled by the catchers
layout: rooms face the courtyard, never the street
badgir sits over the coolest room
breeze or no breeze, the basement is cool
entries.found: Yazd, Kashan, Bam and other desert cities of Iran
entries.notes: The qanat + badgir + courtyard triad is a complete air-conditioning system from the 13th century. Catchers face the prevailing wind.

entries.name: Australian outback homestead
entries.purpose: remote pastoral station headquarters and dwelling
parts: separate meat room, shearing shed nearby
layout: long and low to shed heat
veranda shades every external wall
tanks at the corners, gravity-fed
entries.found: sprawling cattle and sheep stations of the Australian outback
entries.notes: One house per hundred thousand hectares; the mail plane is the school bus. Tanks, verandas and fly screens decide survival.

entries.name: Maasai manyatta
entries.purpose: family hut inside a fortified kraal
parts: low dome of mud and dung
thorn-bush enkang fence ringing the whole camp
layout: women build and own the hut
huts ring a central cattle boma
the enkang thorn fence turns lions and raiders
entries.found: Kenya and northern Tanzania, in pastoral savanna country
entries.notes: Women own the houses; men own the herds. Lions pace the thorn fence at night — the dung-and-mud wall is the armour.

entries.name: Rajasthani haveli
entries.purpose: courtyard mansion of merchant or noble family
parts: jaali screens for shade and privacy
layout: rooms arranged around two or more courtyards
public rooms at front, family at back
the jaali is air conditioning and veiling in one
entries.found: Jaisalmer, Jodhpur, Nawalgarh and other Thar Desert cities
entries.notes: Built with caravan profits; the desert sun bakes the softest stone so carvers loved it. Jaisalmer's yellow sandstone glows twice a day.

entries.name: Tuareg tent (ehan)
parts: low flat canopy of sewn indigo strips
layout: lower and flatter than the black tent
windward side staked low
camel and goats camp close by
entries.found: across the Sahara, Algeria to Niger, Mali and Libya
entries.notes: Indigo cloth rubs blue onto skin and clothes — 'les hommes bleus'. The tent is the woman's property and moves with her.

entries.name: Moroccan ksar
entries.purpose: fortified desert village, dwelling for a whole tribe
layout: a wall you read before you see the village
granary tower at the highest point
family alleys, one gate
entries.found: the Draa and Dades valleys of southern Morocco, e.g. Aït Benhaddou (UNESCO)
entries.notes: The gate is the whole economy: everything comes through one choke point. Film crews love Aït Benhaddou for this reason.

entries.name: Ancestral Puebloan cliff dwelling
entries.purpose: communal cliff dwelling, part of a complex system
parts: sandstone rooms under a rock alcove
layout: rooms stacked into the alcove, 3-4 storeys
access originally by ladder from below
alcove shades summer sun, warms in winter
entries.found: Mesa Verde, Colorado; Canyon de Chelly and other canyons of the Southwest
entries.notes: Built into alcoves for shade and defense, abandoned by about 1300 CE; drought and conflict are the leading suspects. Cliff Palace holds ~150 rooms.

entries.name: Chacoan great house (Pueblo Bonito)
layout: semicircle against the canyon wall
great kivas at the courtyard center
roads run dead straight to other great houses
entries.found: Chaco Canyon, New Mexico, USA (UNESCO)
entries.notes: Not just housing: the center of a road-linked regional system. Every ponderosa beam came from mountains 80 km away — a logistics feat.

entries.name: Cappadocian cave dwelling
materials: soft volcanic tuff excavated from the slope
added stone facade for grand houses
layout: pick the soft rock, carve rooms, fit a facade
rooms share tunnel circulation
whole underground cities exist (Derinkuyu)
entries.found: Göreme, Uçhisar, Zelve, Ürgüp in Cappadocia, Turkey
entries.notes: Derinkuyu goes down 8+ levels with room for ~20,000 people: kitchens, church, stables, ventilation shafts. Rooms hold a steady ~13 C.

entries.name: Chinese yaodong (loess cave dwelling)
parts: sunken courtyard for the dugout type
facade of arches for the cliff type
layout: three types: sunken courtyard, cliff-face, and free-standing vaulted rows
arches march down the cliff face
cave is self-supporting; no formwork
entries.found: the Loess Plateau — Shaanxi, Shanxi, Henan; tens of millions still live in yaodongs
entries.notes: A whole architecture dug not built. Loess stands on its own arches but liquefies in heavy rain — the great enemy of every yaodong.

entries.name: Matmata troglodyte dwelling
parts: roofs at ground level, so fields on top
layout: drop down a ramp into a cool pit
all rooms face the courtyard, not the surface
windmill of light from above
entries.found: the Matmata region of southern Tunisia
entries.notes: The surface is farmland; the house is underneath it. Luke Skywalker's home in Star Wars Episode IV (1977) was Hotel Sidi Driss here.

entries.name: Petra rock-cut dwelling
entries.purpose: tombs repurposed as dwellings; the city was lived in a rock face
parts: cisterns and dams feeding carved channels
layout: adobe houses filled the wadi floor between rock-cut facades
every drop of rain was harvested, carved into dams and cisterns
theater seating carved from rock
entries.found: Petra, Jordan (UNESCO)
entries.notes: Most famous facades were tombs, not homes. The genius of Petra is water: dams, channels and cisterns turned sand into a garden city.

entries.name: Dogon cliff dwelling
entries.purpose: village of dense adobe houses at the foot of the escarpment; caves above were refuges
parts: toguna public shelter with low thick roof
layout: cluster of mudbrick houses at the cliff base
granaries packed tighter than the houses
caves reachable by rope for hiding grain and people
entries.found: the Bandiagara Escarpment, Mali (UNESCO, Pays dogon)
entries.notes: A cliff-foot village with granaries you can stand on and a toguna roof so low you cannot fight under it. Astronomy was part of the architecture.

entries.name: Tata Somba (takyenta)
entries.purpose: fortified family dwelling, granary and shrine in one
parts: two storeys: ground floor stable/store, upper floor rooms
arrow slits and a single entrance
sacred pottery and horns over the door
layout: walls thick enough to stop arrows
central courtyard with meule and mortier sunk in the floor
ladder or carved log staircase to the upper terrace
entries.found: Koutammakou, northwest Benin and northern Togo (UNESCO, since 2004)
entries.notes: Le Corbusier admired them as 'living machines'. Most Tammari still live in one; the form is UNESCO-listed and still built new.

entries.name: Siwan kershef house (Shali style)
materials: kershef (salt-mud blocks from Siwa's salt lakes)
parts: huge salt-mud walls, over a metre thick
multi-storey mass piled into the old Shali fortress
small high windows for cross ventilation
layout: ground floor for goods, family above
guest room at the front, private rooms behind
small high windows, huge thermal mass
entries.found: Shali old town, Siwa oasis, Egypt
entries.notes: Built of salt from the lakes: brilliant insulator, terrible in rain. The 1926 cloudburst collapsed half of Shali in three days.

entries.name: Somali aqal
parts: woven mat covering tied on with rope
packs onto camels when camp moves
layout: dome, low and aerodynamic
assembled by women in hours
herds camp right outside
entries.found: the Somali rangelands — Somalia, Ethiopia (Somali region), Kenya
entries.notes: A house that fits on one camel. The woven mats are both wall and wealth; a new aqal is a prestige purchase.

entries.name: San grass hut (Kalahari)
layout: built in a few hours, abandoned in days
camp shifts with game and water
grass walls against cold Kalahari nights
entries.found: the Kalahari — Botswana, Namibia and South Africa (Bushmanland)
entries.notes: Housing as pure behavior: the San moved camp frequently and valued mobility over durability. Nothing to loot; nothing to defend.

entries.name: Aboriginal Australian humpy (gunyah)
parts: bark slab wall on the windward side
layout: crescent against the wind
open toward the fire
camp follows water and seasonal food
entries.found: arid and semi-arid Australia, camp after camp along dreams and trade routes
entries.notes: Also called gunyah, mia-mia, wiltja (W. Australia). It shelters against weather, not against strangers — there is no door on purpose.

entries.name: Afghan qala (fortified compound)
entries.purpose: fortified family compound for an extended clan
parts: residential rooms around an inner courtyard
stables and store for grain inside
layout: one gate, controlled by the eldest
towers command the walls
family, animals and grain all inside the one wall
entries.found: the valleys and plateaus of Afghanistan and the Iranian/Central Asian fringe
entries.notes: The qala is a castle that is also a village. In bad years it is the only safe place for a whole valley's grain.

entries.name: Arabian barasti hut
parts: palm-frond walls sewn to a pole frame
layout: breeze passes straight through the frond weave
wall of palm trunks or woven mats
kitchen separate, palm shade outside
entries.found: coastal and desert Arabia — UAE (barasti), Oman (areesh)
entries.notes: The poor man's summer palace: hot outside, breathable inside. The permanent winter house was coral stone or adobe ('bait').

entries.name: Najdi mudbrick house (Diriyah style)
entries.purpose: courtyard townhouse of the Najd plateau
layout: rooms around a central court
heavy walls bridge day and night temperature swings
flat roof drying dates in autumn
entries.found: Najd — Diriyah (At-Turaif, UNESCO), Riyadh, Al-Ula, Qassim
entries.notes: At-Turaif is the best-surviving example of the style: entire mudbrick palace-sandcastle town, part museum, part residence.

entries.name: Sardinian stazzo (Gallurese farmhouse)
parts: pitched tile roof, low profile against mistral
layout: fortress-like block, tiny windows
farm yard wired by granite walls
granite gets scorching by day and freezing by night
entries.found: Gallura, northern Sardinia, in oak and granite country
entries.notes: 'Stazzo' is both the farmhouse and the farm. Unrendered granite looks grim until you realize it has been farming there for 300 years.

entries.name: Maltese razzett (farmhouse)
parts: small attached chapel on rich estates
layout: square courtyard core with rooms around
flat roof for drying tomatoes, wheat and washing
fields tiny and walled, everything terraced
entries.found: the Maltese countryside, especially Gozo, in stone-poor fields
entries.notes: Every field is a rubble-walled room; the house is just the biggest one. Limestone dust is everywhere — Maltese stone ages like bread.

entries.name: Canary Island cave dwelling (Artenara style)
parts: rooms carved into the soft tuff slope
facade built in front of the cave mouth
layout: cave behind, facade in front
3-5 m of rock keeps rooms at cave temperature year-round
pueblos of caves march down the ravines
entries.found: Gran Canaria (Artenara, Guayadeque) and Tenerife (Güímar)
entries.notes: Guanches lived in these caves when Europeans arrived; nobody has knocked them down since. Invisible rooms behind every whitewashed door.
